nnn - Supercharge your productivity!

`nnn` (_n³_) is a full-featured terminal file manager. It's tiny, nearly 0-config and incredibly fast. It is designed to be unobtrusive with smart workflows to match the trains of thought. `nnn` can analyze disk usage, batch rename, launch apps and pick files. The plugin repository has tons of plugins to extend the capabilities further e.g. live previews, (un)mount disks, find & list, file/dir diff, upload files. Runs on the Pi, Termux (Android), Linux, macOS, BSD, Haiku, Cygwin, WSL, across DEs or a strictly CLI env. ## Features - Quality - Privacy-aware (no unconfirmed user data collection) - POSIX-compliant - Highly optimized code - Frugal - Typically needs less than 3.5MB resident memory - Works with 8 colors (and xterm 256 colors) - Disk-IO sensitive (few disk reads and writes) - No FPU usage (all integer maths, even for file size) - Minimizes screen refresh with fast line redraws - Tiny binary (typically around 100KB) - 1-column mode for smaller terminals and form factors - Portable - Language-agnostic plugins - Static binary available (no need to install) - Minimal library deps, easy to compile - No config file, minimal config with sensible defaults - Plugin to backup configuration - Widely available on many packagers - Touch enabled, handheld-friendly shortcuts - Unicode support - Modes - Light (default), detail - Disk usage analyzer (block/apparent) - File picker - Navigation - Filter with automatic dir entry on unique match - *Type-to-nav* (turbo navigation/always filter) mode - Jump to an entry with visible relative offset - Contexts (_aka_ tabs/workspaces) with custom colors - Sessions, bookmarks, mark and visit a dir - Remote mounts (needs `sshfs`, `rclone`) - Familiar shortcuts (arrows, ~, -, @), quick look-up - `cd` on quit (*easy* shell integration) - Proceed to next file on file open and selection - Search - Instant filtering with *search-as-you-type* - Fuzzy, regex and string (default) filters - Subtree search plugin to open or edit files - Sort - Ordered pure numeric names by default (visit `/proc`) - Case-insensitive version (_aka_ natural) sort - By name, access/change/mod (default) time, size, extn - Reverse sort - Directory-specific ordering - Mimes - Preview hovered files in FIFO-based previewer - Open with desktop opener or specify a custom opener - File-specific colors (or minimal _dirs in context color_) - Icons and Emojis support (customize and compile-in) - Plugin for image, video and audio thumbnails - Create, list, extract (to), mount (FUSE based) archives - Option to open all text files in `$EDITOR` - Convenience - Detailed file stats and mime information - Run plugins and custom commands with hotkeys - FreeDesktop compliant trash utility integration - Cross-dir file/all/range selection - Create (with parents), rename, duplicate files and dirs - Create new file or directory (tree) on startup - Batch renamer for selection or dir - List input stream of file paths from stdin or plugin - Copy (as), move (as), delete, archive, link selection - Easily copy, move paths in system clipboard to current dir - Dir updates, notification on `cp`, `mv`, `rm` completion - Copy file paths to system clipboard on select - Launch apps, run commands, spawn a shell, toggle exe - Access context paths/files at prompt or spawned shell - Lock terminal after configurable idle timeout - Capture and show output of a program in help screen - Basic support for screen readers and braille displays ## Usage Don't memorize! Arrows, /, q suffice. Tab creates and/or cycles contexts. ? lists shortcuts. For detailed usage instructions, command-line options, and configuration information, please refer to the man page (`man nnn`) or visit the project Wiki. ## Installation `nnn` is available on many package managers. Install it using your distribution's package manager, or download a pre-built static binary. Common installation methods: - **Arch Linux**: `pacman -S nnn` - **Debian/Ubuntu**: `apt install nnn` - **Fedora**: `dnf install nnn` - **macOS (Homebrew)**: `brew install nnn` - **FreeBSD**: `pkg install nnn` For more installation options and detailed instructions, visit the project Wiki. ## License BSD 2-Clause License Copyright © 2016-2026 Arun Prakash Jana and contributors See LICENSE file for full license text. ========== BSD 2-Clause License Copyright (c) 2014-2016, Lazaros Koromilas Copyright (c) 2014-2016, Dimitris Papastamos Copyright (c) 2016-2026, Arun Prakash Jana All rights reserved. THIS SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED BY THE COPYRIGHT HOLDERS AND CONTRIBUTORS "AS IS" AND ANY EXPRESS OR IMPLIED WARRANTIES, INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, THE IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY AND FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE ARE DISCLAIMED. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE COPYRIGHT HOLDER OR CONTRIBUTORS BE LIABLE FOR ANY DIRECT, INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY, OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES (INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, PROCUREMENT OF SUBSTITUTE GOODS OR SERVICES; LOSS OF USE, DATA, OR PROFITS; OR BUSINESS INTERRUPTION) HOWEVER CAUSED AND ON ANY THEORY OF LIABILITY, WHETHER IN CONTRACT, STRICT LIABILITY, OR TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE OR OTHERWISE) ARISING IN ANY WAY OUT OF THE USE OF THIS SOFTWARE, EVEN IF ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGE. ========== .Dd Feb 14, 2026 .Dt NNN 1 .Os .Sh NAME .Nm nnn .Nd The unorthodox terminal file manager. .Sh SYNOPSIS .Nm .Op Ar -aAcCdDeEfgHJKnQrRSuUVxz0h .Op Ar -b key .Op Ar -F val .Op Ar -l val .Op Ar -p file .Op Ar -P key .Op Ar -s name .Op Ar -t secs .Op Ar -T key .Op Ar PATH .Sh DESCRIPTION .Nm .Pq Nnn's Not Noice is a performance-optimized, feature-packed terminal file manager with seamless desktop integration, simplified navigation, .Em type-to-nav mode with dir auto-enter, disk usage analyzer mode, bookmarks, contexts, application launcher, familiar navigation shortcuts, subshell spawning and much more. It remains a simple and efficient file manager that stays out of your way. .Pp .Nm opens the current working directory if .Ar PATH is not specified. If .Ar PATH is specified and it exists, .Nm will open it. If the .Ar PATH doesn't exist and ends with a \fB/\fR, .Nm will attempt to create the directory tree and open it. Otherwise, .Ar PATH is considered a path to a regular file and .Nm attempts to create the complete directory tree to the file, open the parent directory and prompt to create the new file in it with the base filename. .Sh OPTIONS For detailed command-line options and flags, please refer to the full documentation or run .Nm with the .Fl h flag to see available options. .Sh SEE ALSO For more information, visit the project homepage or Wiki. .Sh AUTHORS .An Arun Prakash Jana Aq Mt engineerarun@gmail.com .Pp and contributors.

import subprocess, time, sys, os

SESSION = "probe"
COLS = int(os.environ.get("COLS", "100"))
ROWS = int(os.environ.get("ROWS", "30"))

def sh(cmd):
    return subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout

def kill():
    sh("tmux kill-server 2>/dev/null")

def start():
    kill()
    sh(f"tmux new-session -d -s {SESSION} -x {COLS} -y {ROWS} 'bash /tmp/lab/keyprobe.sh'")
    time.sleep(1.2)

def cap():
    return sh(f"tmux capture-pane -t {SESSION} -p")

def send(*keys):
    k = " ".join(f"'{x}'" if len(x)==1 else x for x in keys)
    sh(f"tmux send-keys -t {SESSION} {k}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    keys = sys.argv[1]
    start()
    for c in keys:
        send(c)
        time.sleep(0.35)
        print("=== KEY", repr(c))
        print(cap())
        send("Escape")
        time.sleep(0.25)
PYEOF
echo written

import subprocess, time, sys, os

def send(*keys):

    sh(f"tmux send-keys -t {SESSION} {k}")

out = []
chars = sys.argv[1]

    send("q")
    time.sleep(0.3)
    print("=== KEY", repr(c))
    print("--- after")
    print(s1)
    print("--- after escape")
    print(s2)
PYEOF

import subprocess, time, sys, os

SESSION = "probe"
COLS = int(os.environ.get("COLS", "100"))
ROWS = int(os.environ.get("ROWS", "30"))

def sh(cmd):
    return subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout

def send(*keys):
    k = " ".join(f"'{x}'" if len(x)==1 else x for x in keys)
    sh(f"tmux send-keys -t {SESSION} {k}")

def compact(s):
    lines = s.split("\n")
    # header line 0, entries = lines 2.., last 3 lines
    hdr = lines[0]
    mid = [l for l in lines[2:-3] if l.strip()]
    tail = lines[-3:]
    return "HDR: " + hdr + "\nMID: " + " | ".join(mid) + "\nTAIL: " + " || ".join(tail)

for c in sys.argv[1]:
    sh("bash /tmp/lab/mkscratch.sh")
    sh("tmux kill-server 2>/dev/null")
    sh(f"tmux new-session -d -s {SESSION} -x {COLS} -y {ROWS} 'bash /tmp/lab/keyprobe.sh'")
    time.sleep(1.2)
    send(c)
    time.sleep(0.4)
    s1 = sh(f"tmux capture-pane -t {SESSION} -p")
    send("Escape")
    time.sleep(0.3)
    s2 = sh(f"tmux capture-pane -t {SESSION} -p")
    print("=== KEY", repr(c))
    print(compact(s1))
    if s2 != s1:
        print("(after esc): " + compact(s2))
PYEOF

def send(*keys):

import subprocess, time, sys, os
SESSION = "probe"
COLS = int(os.environ.get("COLS", "100")); ROWS = int(os.environ.get("ROWS", "30"))
def sh(cmd): return subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
def send(*keys):
    k = " ".join(f"'{x}'" if len(x)==1 else x for x in keys); sh(f"tmux send-keys -t {SESSION} {k}")
def full(s): return "\n".join(l for l in s.split("\n"))
for c in sys.argv[1]:
    sh("bash /tmp/lab/mkscratch.sh"); sh("tmux kill-server 2>/dev/null")
    sh(f"tmux new-session -d -s {SESSION} -x {COLS} -y {ROWS} 'bash /tmp/lab/keyprobe.sh'")
    time.sleep(1.2)
    send(*sys.argv[2:])
    time.sleep(0.4)
    send(c)
    time.sleep(0.5)
    s1 = sh(f"tmux capture-pane -t {SESSION} -p")
    send("Escape"); time.sleep(0.3)
    s2 = sh(f"tmux capture-pane -t {SESSION} -p")
    print("=== KEY", repr(c), "prefix:", repr(sys.argv[2:]))
    print(full(s1))
    if s2 != s1:
        print("(after esc): " + full(s2))
PYEOF
cd /tmp/lab && python3 probe4.py "G" 2>&1 | head -40

import subprocess, time, sys, os

    sh(f"tmux send-keys -t {SESSION} " + " ".join(keys))

    time.sleep(1.3)
    return sh(f"tmux capture-pane -t {SESSION} -p")
def capture(): return sh(f"tmux capture-pane -t {SESSION} -p")
def difflines(a,b):
    la, lb = a.split("\n"), b.split("\n"); out=[]
    for i in range(max(len(la),len(lb))):
        x = la[i] if i<len(la) else ""; y = lb[i] if i<len(lb) else ""
        if x!=y: out.append(f"L{i+1}: {y!r}  (was {x!r})")
    return out
def keyprobe(keys, delay=0.45, show=True, pre=None):
    base = restart()
    if pre:
        send(pre); time.sleep(delay); base = capture()
    for k in keys:
        send(k); time.sleep(delay)
        s = capture(); d = difflines(base, s)
        print(f"--- after {k!r}:")
        for l in d: print("   ", l)
        if not d: print("    (no change)")
        base = s

        print(f"--- after {k!r}:")
        for l in d: print("   ", l)
        if not d: print("    (no change)")
        s = n
    if snapshot:
        subprocess.run("ls -la /tmp/scratch", shell=True)

    if base is None and args=='':
        base=c
        print(c[:600])

        print([x[:120] for x in d] or '(no change)')
PYEOF"}

# nnn reimplementation - handoff report

## What this is
A from-scratch C reimplementation of the `nnn` terminal file manager (v5.2), derived
purely from *behavioural observation* of the provided `./executable` (tmux-driven key
probing, no disassembly, no source lookup).

## Layout
- `src/nnn.h`      - types (struct entry/ctx), constants
- `src/core.c`     - globals, string/size helpers, sorting, dir reading, filter,
                     selection bookkeeping, colour handling
- `src/includes.h` - cross-file declarations
- `src/extra.c`    - entry suffix, date/perm formatting, listing window, misc globals
- `src/render.c`   - header (8-context indicator), entry rows, status line
- `src/prompts.c`  - generic text input + filter prompt (with `str/reg/fzy` hint line)
- `src/ops.c`      - external command runner + cp/mv/rm/tar/editor operations
- `src/browse.c`   - key loop, all prompts/operations, session+selection persistence, CLI/main
- `compile.sh`     - concatenates the above into `nnn_all.c` and builds `./executable`
                     with `gcc -O2 -lncurses` (libncurses-dev is preinstalled)

## Verified behaviours implemented
* CLI: `-h` usage text (verbatim), `-V` -> `5.2\n`; getopt errors print
  `<argv0>: invalid option -- 'x'` to stderr and the usage to stdout, exit 1.
  `-F` only accepts 0/1, `-T` only a/d/e/r/s/t/v (else silent exit 1).
* Startup: creates `~/.config/nnn/{bookmarks,mounts,plugins,sessions}`,
  loads `~/.config/nnn/.selection` (NUL-separated paths).
* 8 contexts cycled with Tab (header shows `1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8`, active = bold+reverse,
  visited = bold+underline, cwd underlined+blue, `~` abbreviates $HOME).
* Light/detail modes (`d` / `-d`): detail = `>YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM  perms  size(9 wide)  name`.
* Status line: `cur/total ` [+`<mark>*`/`+N` reverse] ` ` flags(`HEMSVR`) ` `
